sentence: This project studies how subterranean termites cope with changes in soil moisture and temperature, and the molecular changes behind this.
This project uses observations made during a total solar eclipse to study the magnetic fields, hot plasma and solar wind of the solar corona.
This project builds a way to control systems described by partial differential equations by using measured data.
This project builds a platform that quickly updates large deep learning models as conditions change, without slow retraining.
This project tests whether short oligonucleotides joined to small molecules can turn genes on or off as a form of gene therapy.
This project tests whether machine learning can improve how weather models use radar observations to forecast severe storms.
This project builds drones and ground robots with sensors and artificial intelligence that find diseases in apple orchards and spray pesticides only where needed.
This project carries out summer research in astrophysics, atomic and molecular physics, condensed matter physics, and high energy physics.
This project builds mathematical and computational tools to compare complex data such as images, shapes and networks.
This project supports a meeting where researchers share their work on the model plant Arabidopsis thaliana.
This project studies how nitrogen-fixing Frankia bacteria in alder roots affect leaf chemistry and the herbivores that feed on the trees.
This project builds a quiet, compact MRI scanner for the head that works without loud gradient coils.
This project compares computer models that predict temperatures in metal parts made by 3D printing, using measurements from printed parts.
This project studies a nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria species from warm ocean waters and how it responds to temperature and low nutrients.
This project covers laboratory research in nanomanufacturing methods such as photolithography, 3D printing, electron microscopy and nanofabrication.
This project develops statistical methods to study quantum learning, including learning quantum states and a model called Boson sampling.
This project studies how tiny protein machines called nanomotors turn energy into motion and how they adapt to different conditions.
